<description>
`FlushStateToDisk()` handles block storage directly. It applies `BlockManager`'s prune locks, writes its pruned flag, checks its blocks directory space and runs the flush, index write and file deletion, while `BlockManager` reads the chainstate to pick files. A pruning API on block storage (#35627) would have to go through validation for all of it.

This moves the storage side into `BlockManager`, as described in the same issue. Validation decides which heights may be pruned and passes them as limits. `BlockManager` applies its prune locks, selects the files, flushes, writes the index and deletes the files, in the same order as before. There is no behavior change to my knowledge.

Based on #36735

Thanks to musaHaruna for his [review on my fork](https://github.com/pzafonte/bitcoin/pull/2#pullrequestreview-5533305792), which led to grouping and checking the prune limits and to moving the prune bookkeeping into `BlockManager`.
</description>

<commits>
24ad36d929 test: apply BlockManager args in test fixtures

Without this, -prune and -fastprune in extra_args have no effect.

2334d27a24 test: check flush retry after failure

Move the blk file aside instead of deleting it, so it can be restored.

108d7ff03c test: characterize a failed prune flush

The pruned blk/rev files are not deleted, even after a later flush
succeeds.

d224fb8721 validation: delete pruned files on a later flush

Files selected for pruning were kept in a local, so a failed flush left
them on disk until the next startup.

Keep them in BlockManager and delete them after the next block index
write. Take them with the dirty entries, which WriteBlockIndexDB() drops
even if the write fails. Drop a file from the set once a block is
written to it.

Pending files wait for the next periodic, forced or shutdown flush
rather than forcing one, which would retry a failing write on every
block.

fb911aecde refactor: let BlockManager write block storage

Move the block and undo file flush, block index write and pruned file
deletion from FlushStateToDisk into BlockManager. Their bench log lines
change from FlushStateToDisk to WriteBlockStorage.

14de6dfdf5 refactor: apply prune locks in BlockManager

Validation read BlockManager's prune locks directly. Move that code and
PRUNE_LOCK_BUFFER into BlockManager.

ae7d92d02e refactor: pass prune limits to BlockManager

BlockManager read the chainstate to decide what to prune. Decide in
validation and pass the height range and sizes instead. An Assume checks
the heights are non-negative.

777b2f90de refactor: move prune bookkeeping into BlockManager

Move FlushStateToDisk's handling of the prune request, prune locks,
pruned flag, files to delete and blocks directory space check into
BlockManager. The prune request is cleared before the prune locks are
applied rather than after selection, which differs only if selection
throws.

An Assume checks that the pruned flag is set before files are queued
for deletion, so a restart knows blocks were deleted.
</commits>
